spine.name: Adam
spine.bio: Adam is the first man, formed by God from the dust of the ground and given the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). He was placed in the Garden of Eden to dress and keep it, and he named every beast and fowl that God brought before him (Genesis 2:19-20). From his side God made Eve, his wife; together they ate of the forbidden tree at the serpent's temptation, and by this fall sin and death entered the world and they were driven from Eden (Genesis 3). He lived 930 years and became the father of humanity, including Cain, Abel, and Seth (Genesis 5:5).

spine.name: Seth
spine.bio: Seth is the third named son of Adam and Eve, appointed by God as a replacement for the slain Abel; Eve declared, 'God hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew' (Genesis 4:25). He became the father of Enos, and in his days men began to call upon the name of the LORD (Genesis 4:26). Through Seth ran the godly line of the faithful that led to Noah and ultimately to Christ. He lived 912 years (Genesis 5:8).

spine.name: Enos
spine.bio: Enos is the son of Seth and grandson of Adam, born when Seth was 105 (Genesis 5:6). In his day 'began men to call upon the name of the LORD' (Genesis 4:26). He fathered Cainan and lived 905 years (Genesis 5:11).

spine.name: Cainan
spine.disambig: son of Enos; distinct from the Cainan of Luke 3:36 (son of Arphaxad, not in the Hebrew Masoretic Genesis 10-11 line)
spine.bio: Cainan is the son of Enos in the line of Seth, born when Enos was ninety years old (Genesis 5:9). He fathered Mahalaleel and lived 910 years (Genesis 5:14). He is known only as a link in the antediluvian genealogy from Adam to Noah, with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Mahalaleel
spine.bio: Mahalaleel, whose name means 'praise of God,' is the son of Cainan in the Sethite line (Genesis 5:12). He fathered Jared and lived 895 years (Genesis 5:17). He is known only as a link in the genealogy from Adam to Noah.

spine.name: Jared
spine.bio: Jared is the son of Mahalaleel and the father of Enoch, born when Mahalaleel was sixty-five (Genesis 5:15-18). He lived 962 years, one of the longest lifespans recorded (Genesis 5:20). Apart from his place in the Sethite genealogy and his fathering of the godly Enoch, no further deeds are recorded of him.

spine.name: Enoch
spine.disambig: son of Jared; the patriarch of the Enoch tradition (1/2/3 Enoch), distinct from Enoch son of Cain (Genesis 4:17-18)
spine.bio: Enoch, the son of Jared and seventh from Adam, is one of Scripture's most extraordinary figures because he 'walked with God: and he was not; for God took him' (Genesis 5:24), being translated so that he did not see death (Hebrews 11:5). He fathered Methuselah and walked with God 300 years, living 365 years in all (Genesis 5:22-23). Jude cites his prophecy that the Lord would come with ten thousands of his saints to execute judgment (Jude 14-15), and a rich later Enoch tradition grew around him. He is remembered above all for his intimate, unbroken fellowship with God.

spine.name: Methuselah
spine.disambig: son of Enoch (Jared's line); the longest-lived figure in the text
spine.bio: Methuselah, son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah, holds the record as the longest-lived human in Scripture, dying at 969 years (Genesis 5:27). He fathered Lamech and stands as a symbol of the great antediluvian lifespans. His death coincides with the era of the Flood in the biblical chronology.

spine.name: Lamech
spine.disambig: son of Methuselah, Noah's father; distinct from Lamech son of Methusael (Genesis 4:18-24), Cain's line
spine.bio: Lamech is the son of Methuselah and the father of Noah, whom he named saying, 'This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the LORD hath cursed' (Genesis 5:29). He lived 777 years (Genesis 5:31). He is distinguished from the earlier Lamech of Cain's line, who boasted of vengeance.

spine.name: Noah
spine.bio: Noah is the tenth from Adam, a man who 'found grace in the eyes of the LORD' and was 'a just man and perfect in his generations,' who walked with God (Genesis 6:8-9). Commanded to build an ark of gopher wood, he preserved his family and pairs of every living creature through the Flood that God sent to judge a corrupt earth (Genesis 6-8). After the waters receded, God set the rainbow as the sign of an everlasting covenant never again to destroy all flesh by flood (Genesis 9:11-17). Noah planted a vineyard, fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth from whom the nations sprang, and lived 950 years (Genesis 9:20, 9:29).

spine.name: Shem
spine.bio: Shem is a son of Noah, singled out for blessing when Noah declared, 'Blessed be the LORD God of Shem' (Genesis 9:26). He honored his father by covering his nakedness with Japheth (Genesis 9:23). He is the ancestor of the Semitic peoples and, through Arphaxad, of Eber, Abraham, and ultimately Israel and Christ (Genesis 11:10-26). He lived 600 years (Genesis 11:11).

spine.name: Arphaxad
spine.bio: Arphaxad is a son of Shem, born two years after the Flood (Genesis 11:10). He fathered Salah and lived 438 years (Genesis 11:12-13). He is a link in the genealogy from Shem to Abraham.

spine.name: Salah
spine.bio: Salah is the son of Arphaxad and father of Eber in the line of Shem (Genesis 11:13-14). He lived 433 years. He is known only as a link in the genealogy from Shem to Abraham.

spine.name: Eber
spine.disambig: eponym of 'Hebrew'
spine.bio: Eber is the son of Salah and father of Peleg, and the ancestral namesake associated with the Hebrews (Genesis 11:14-16). In his son Peleg's days the earth was divided. He lived 464 years and stands as a notable link in the Semitic genealogy.

spine.name: Peleg
spine.bio: Peleg, whose name means 'division,' is the son of Eber, and Scripture notes that 'in his days was the earth divided' (Genesis 10:25), often linked to the scattering of peoples after Babel. He fathered Reu and lived 239 years (Genesis 11:18-19).

spine.name: Reu
spine.bio: Reu is the son of Peleg and father of Serug in the line of Shem (Genesis 11:18-20). He lived 239 years. He is known only as a link in the genealogy from Eber to Abraham.

spine.name: Serug
spine.bio: Serug is the son of Reu and father of Nahor in the line leading to Abraham (Genesis 11:20-22). He lived 230 years. He is known only as a link in this genealogy.

spine.name: Nahor
spine.disambig: father of Terah; distinct from Nahor son of Terah (Genesis 11:26), his own grandson and namesake
spine.bio: Nahor is the son of Serug and the father of Terah, and thus the grandfather of Abraham (Genesis 11:22-24). He lived 148 years. He is known only as a link in the genealogy from Serug to Abraham, and is distinguished from his grandson Nahor, Abraham's brother.

spine.name: Terah
spine.bio: Terah is the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran (Genesis 11:26-27). He set out from Ur of the Chaldees toward the land of Canaan with Abram and Lot but settled in Haran, where he died at 205 years (Genesis 11:31-32). Joshua later records that Terah served other gods beyond the River (Joshua 24:2).

spine.name: Abram
spine.meaning: Abram: exalted father; Abraham: father of a multitude/many nations
spine.disambig: renamed Abraham in Genesis 17:5 ('a father of many nations have I made thee') -- kept under this original term_id for referential continuity with the Phase 1 genealogy chain
spine.bio: Abram, renamed Abraham ('father of many nations'), is called by God out of Ur of the Chaldees with the promise, 'I will make of thee a great nation' (Genesis 12:1-3). God cut an everlasting covenant with him, promising the land of Canaan and descendants as the stars, sealed by circumcision (Genesis 15, 17). His faith was counted to him for righteousness (Genesis 15:6), supremely proven when he obeyed God's command to offer his son Isaac, whom God spared by providing a ram (Genesis 22). Father of the faithful and friend of God, he is the patriarch through whom all families of the earth are blessed, dying at 175 years (Genesis 25:7-8).

spine.name: Isaac
spine.disambig: son of Abraham and Sarah; the child of the covenant
spine.bio: Isaac, whose name means 'he laughs,' is the child of promise born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age (Genesis 21:1-3). He was bound upon the altar in obedience to God and spared by divine provision (Genesis 22). He married Rebekah, fathered the twins Esau and Jacob, and reconfirmed the covenant, prospering greatly in the land (Genesis 24-26). Blind in old age, he blessed Jacob, and he died at 180 years (Genesis 27, 35:28-29).

spine.name: Jacob
spine.meaning: he grasps the heel / supplanter; Israel: he strives with God (Gen 32:28, text-implied)
spine.disambig: younger twin son of Isaac and Rebekah; renamed Israel in Genesis 32:28, confirmed again 35:10 -- kept under this original term_id for referential continuity
spine.bio: Jacob, later named Israel, is the younger twin of Esau who grasped his brother's heel at birth and later obtained both the birthright and the blessing (Genesis 25:26, 27). Fleeing to Haran, he saw the vision of the ladder reaching to heaven (Genesis 28:12), served Laban for Leah and Rachel, and fathered twelve sons who became the tribes of Israel. Returning home, he wrestled through the night with a divine man at Peniel and was renamed Israel, 'for as a prince hast thou power with God' (Genesis 32:24-28). He went down to Egypt in his old age to Joseph, blessed his sons prophetically, and died at 147 years (Genesis 47-49).

spine.name: Judah
spine.disambig: fourth son of Jacob and Leah
spine.bio: Judah, whose name means 'praise,' is the fourth son of Jacob and Leah, and the tribe from which kings and the Messiah would come (Genesis 29:35). He persuaded his brothers to sell Joseph rather than kill him, and later offered himself as surety for Benjamin (Genesis 37, 44). Through his daughter-in-law Tamar he fathered Pharez and Zarah (Genesis 38). Jacob's blessing declared, 'The sceptre shall not depart from Judah... until Shiloh come' (Genesis 49:10), marking Judah as the royal and messianic line.

spine.name: Pharez
spine.disambig: son of Judah and Tamar
spine.bio: Pharez (Perez), whose name means 'a breach,' is the son of Judah by Tamar, born as a twin with Zarah in a striking birth where he 'broke forth' first (Genesis 38:27-30). He is an ancestor of Boaz, David, and Christ (Ruth 4:18, Matthew 1:3). He fathered Hezron and Hamul.

spine.name: Hezron
spine.disambig: son of Pharez, grandson of Judah; distinct from Hezron son of Reuben (Genesis 46:9)
spine.bio: Hezron is a son of Pharez who went down into Egypt with Jacob's household (Genesis 46:12). He is an ancestor of David through his son Ram (Ruth 4:18-19). Beyond his place in the royal genealogy, no further deeds are recorded of him.

spine.name: Ram
spine.disambig: son of Hezron, of the line of Pharez; father of Amminadab; distinct from Ram, an ancestor of Elihu in the book of Job (Job 32:2, not yet catalogued)
spine.bio: Ram (Aram) is the son of Hezron and father of Amminadab in the line from Judah to David (Ruth 4:19, Matthew 1:3-4). He is known only as a link in the messianic genealogy, with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Amminadab
spine.disambig: father of Elisheba and Naashon
spine.bio: Amminadab is the son of Ram and father of Nahshon; his daughter Elisheba married Aaron the high priest (Exodus 6:23). He stands in the royal line from Judah to David (Ruth 4:19-20). Beyond these genealogical connections, no further deeds are recorded of him.

spine.name: Naashon
spine.disambig: son of Amminadab; brother of Elisheba
spine.bio: Naashon (Nahshon), son of Amminadab, was the prince and captain of the tribe of Judah during the wilderness wanderings, leading its offerings and its host (Numbers 1:7, 2:3, 7:12). Brother-in-law to Aaron, he is an ancestor of Boaz and David (Ruth 4:20). He is one of the more identifiable figures in this stretch of the royal line.

spine.name: Salmon
spine.disambig: son of Nahshon; father of Boaz
spine.bio: Salmon is the son of Nahshon and father of Boaz in the line of Judah (Ruth 4:20-21). According to Matthew 1:5 he was the husband of Rahab. He is an ancestor of David and Christ, otherwise known only within this genealogy.

spine.name: Boaz
spine.disambig: a wealthy kinsman of Elimelech, of Bethlehem; redeemed Naomi's land and married Ruth
spine.bio: Boaz is a wealthy and honorable man of Bethlehem, kinsman of Elimelech, who shows favor to the Moabite widow Ruth as she gleans in his fields (Ruth 2). Acting as kinsman-redeemer, he purchases the inheritance of the dead and takes Ruth as his wife (Ruth 4:9-10). Their son Obed became the grandfather of King David, making Boaz a direct ancestor of the royal and messianic line (Ruth 4:17, 21-22).

spine.name: Obed
spine.disambig: son of Boaz and Ruth; father of Jesse; grandfather of David
spine.bio: Obed is the son of Boaz and Ruth, born to continue the name of the dead and hailed by the women of Bethlehem as a restorer of life (Ruth 4:14-17). He is the father of Jesse and grandfather of King David. Beyond this pivotal place in the genealogy, no further deeds are recorded of him.

spine.name: Jesse
spine.disambig: son of Obed; father of David
spine.bio: Jesse is a Bethlehemite of the tribe of Judah, the son of Obed and the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom is David (1 Samuel 16:1, 10-13). Samuel came to his house to anoint the future king from among his sons. Isaiah prophesied of a 'rod out of the stem of Jesse' and 'a root of Jesse' as a messianic ensign to the nations (Isaiah 11:1, 10).

spine.name: David
spine.disambig: youngest son of Jesse; anointed by Samuel; slew Goliath; Israel's second king
spine.bio: David, whose name means 'beloved,' is the youngest son of Jesse, anointed by Samuel as king while still a shepherd boy, upon whom the Spirit of the LORD came (1 Samuel 16:13). He slew the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone in the name of the LORD of hosts (1 Samuel 17), and after years fleeing Saul became king over all Israel, capturing Jerusalem and bringing up the ark (2 Samuel 5-6). A man after God's own heart and the sweet psalmist of Israel, he authored many Psalms, yet also sinned gravely with Bathsheba and repented deeply (2 Samuel 11-12, Psalm 51). God covenanted that his throne would be established for ever, the promise fulfilled in Christ, the Son of David (2 Samuel 7:12-16).

spine.name: Nathan
spine.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem; distinct from Nathan the prophet (2 Samuel 7:2)
spine.bio: Nathan is a son of David and Bathsheba, born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:14). Luke traces Jesus' genealogy through this Nathan rather than through Solomon (Luke 3:31). He is distinguished from Nathan the prophet, and beyond his place in the royal line no personal deeds are recorded of him.

spine.name: Mattatha
spine.disambig: son of Nathan, a son of David; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:31)
spine.bio: Mattatha is the son of Nathan in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:31). He is known only as a link in that chain, with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Menan
spine.disambig: son of Mattatha; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:31)
spine.bio: Menan (Menna) appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:31), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Melea
spine.disambig: son of Menan; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:31)
spine.bio: Melea appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:31), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Eliakim
spine.disambig: son of Melea; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:30); a real, distinct third Eliakim from Hezekiah's steward (2 Kings 18, Phase 12) and Matthew's own post-exilic Eliakim, son of Abiud (Matthew 1:13, Phase 38)
spine.bio: This Eliakim is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:30), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from other men named Eliakim in Scripture.

spine.name: Jonan
spine.disambig: son of Eliakim; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:30)
spine.bio: Jonan appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:30), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Joseph
spine.disambig: son of Jonan; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:30); distinct from every other already-catalogued man named Joseph, including two others in this same genealogy
spine.bio: This Joseph is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph the husband of Mary (Luke 3:30), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from Joseph the patriarch and Joseph of Nazareth.

spine.name: Juda
spine.disambig: son of Joseph; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:30); distinct from the patriarch Judah and from another Juda in this same genealogy
spine.bio: This Juda is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:30), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from Judah the patriarch.

spine.name: Simeon
spine.disambig: son of Juda; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:30); distinct from the patriarch Simeon (Genesis 29:33, Phase 3) and from Simeon the devout (Luke 2:25, Phase 43)
spine.bio: This Simeon is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:30), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from Simeon the patriarch and Simeon of Luke 2.

spine.name: Levi
spine.disambig: son of Simeon; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:29); distinct from the patriarch Levi and from another Levi in this same genealogy
spine.bio: This Levi is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:29), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from Levi the patriarch.

spine.disambig: son of Levi; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:29); distinct from another Matthat in this same genealogy
spine.bio: This Matthat appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:29), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Jorim
spine.disambig: son of Matthat; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:29)
spine.bio: Jorim appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:29), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Eliezer
spine.disambig: son of Jorim; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:29); distinct from Eliezer of Damascus (Genesis 15:2), Eliezer son of Moses (Exodus 18:4), and Eliezer son of Dodavah (2 Chronicles 20:37)
spine.bio: This Eliezer is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:29), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from other men named Eliezer in Scripture.

spine.name: Jose
spine.disambig: son of Eliezer; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:29)
spine.bio: Jose (Joshua/Jesus in some texts) appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:29), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Er
spine.disambig: son of Jose; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:28); distinct from Er, firstborn son of Judah (Genesis 38:3, Phase 3)
spine.bio: This Er is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:28), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from Er the firstborn son of Judah.

spine.name: Elmodam
spine.disambig: son of Er; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:28)
spine.bio: Elmodam (Elmadam) appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:28), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Cosam
spine.disambig: son of Elmodam; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:28)
spine.bio: Cosam appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:28), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Addi
spine.disambig: son of Cosam; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:28)
spine.bio: Addi appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:28), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Melchi
spine.disambig: son of Addi; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:28); distinct from another Melchi in this same genealogy
spine.bio: This Melchi is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:28), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Neri
spine.disambig: son of Melchi; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:27)
spine.bio: Neri appears in Luke's genealogy as the father of Salathiel (Luke 3:27), otherwise known only as a link in the chain from David to Joseph, with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Salathiel
spine.disambig: son of Neri, per Luke's own genealogy (3:27) -- a real, long-debated question (traced at least to Julius Africanus) asks whether this is the same Salathiel already catalogued as son of Jeconiah in the Solomonic line (Phase 16), reconciled by a levirate marriage or a legal-vs-biological distinction between the two gospels' genealogies, or a different man who happens to share the name one generation before a son also named Zorobabel. Not merged; disclosed as a real, open question
spine.bio: Salathiel (Shealtiel) is the father of Zorobabel in the genealogies (Luke 3:27, Matthew 1:12). He lived in the era of the Babylonian captivity and stands in the line leading to Joseph. Beyond his place in the genealogy his deeds are not detailed.

spine.name: Zorobabel
spine.disambig: son of Salathiel, per Luke's own genealogy (3:27) -- the same real, long-debated question as his own father: whether this is the already-catalogued Zerubbabel, son of Pedaiah, who led the return from Babylon (Phase 22), or a different man of the same name. Not merged; disclosed as a real, open question
spine.bio: Zorobabel (Zerubbabel), son of Salathiel, is the governor of Judah who led the return of the exiles from Babylon and laid the foundation of the second temple, encouraged by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah (Ezra 3, Haggai 1-2). He appears in both Matthew's and Luke's genealogies of Christ (Matthew 1:12-13, Luke 3:27). He is one of the more historically prominent post-exilic figures in the line.

spine.name: Rhesa
spine.disambig: son of Zorobabel; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:27) -- some scholars read "Rhesa" as an Aramaic title ("resha," prince/head) attached to Zorobabel rather than a separate person's own name; this project follows the KJV's own plain reading of it as a distinct name, disclosing the alternate reading here rather than adopting it
spine.bio: Rhesa appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph, listed after Zorobabel (Luke 3:27), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Joanna
spine.disambig: son of Rhesa; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:27) -- a real, distinct man from the woman disciple of the same English spelling appearing later in this Gospel (8:3, a future phase)
spine.bio: Joanna (Joannan) appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:27), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from the woman Joanna of Luke 8:3.

spine.name: Juda
spine.disambig: son of Joanna; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:26); distinct from the patriarch Judah and from another Juda in this same genealogy

spine.name: Joseph
spine.disambig: son of Juda; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:26); distinct from every other already-catalogued man named Joseph, including two others in this same genealogy

spine.name: Semei
spine.disambig: son of Joseph; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:26)
spine.bio: Semei (Semein) appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:26), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Mattathias
spine.disambig: son of Semei; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:26); distinct from another Mattathias in this same genealogy
spine.bio: This Mattathias is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:26), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.bio: Maath appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:26), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.bio: Naum appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:25), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from the prophet Nahum.

spine.disambig: son of Naum; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:25); a real, distinct man from the prophet Amos of Tekoa (Phase 28), who lived centuries earlier
spine.bio: This Amos is known only as a link in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:25), with no further recorded deeds. He is distinct from the prophet Amos.

spine.name: Mattathias
spine.disambig: son of Amos; an ancestor of Jesus in Luke's own genealogy (3:25); distinct from another Mattathias in this same genealogy

spine.name: Joseph

spine.bio: Janna (Jannai) appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy from David to Joseph (Luke 3:24), with no further recorded deeds.

spine.name: Matthat

spine.name: Heli
spine.disambig: son of Matthat; father of Joseph, husband of Mary, per Luke's own genealogy (3:23) -- a real, direct conflict with Matthew 1:16 (Phase 38), which names Joseph's father as Jacob. Joseph's own already-catalogued lineage row records Matthew's claim (father_term_id = Jacob) and is deliberately left unchanged here; this conflict is disclosed on Heli's own entry, not resolved either way. (Ancient harmonizations exist -- Heli as Mary's own father, "son" meaning son-in-law; or a levirate marriage between half-brothers Jacob and Heli -- neither adopted by this project.)
spine.bio: Heli is named in Luke's genealogy as the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary (Luke 3:23); many understand him as the father of Mary in this line. Beyond this position at the near end of the genealogy of Christ, no further deeds are recorded of him.

BIBLE:Adam.name: Abel
BIBLE:Adam.bio: Abel is the second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep whose offering of the firstlings of his flock God accepted, while rejecting Cain's (Genesis 4:2-4). His righteousness provoked his brother's envy, and Cain slew him in the field, making Abel the first martyr, whose blood cried out from the ground (Genesis 4:8-10). Jesus called him 'righteous Abel,' and Hebrews says that by faith 'he being dead yet speaketh' (Matthew 23:35, Hebrews 11:4).

BIBLE:Adam.name: Cain
BIBLE:Adam.bio: Cain is the firstborn son of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the ground whose offering God did not respect (Genesis 4:1-5). Consumed by anger and refusing to master sin, he rose up and murdered his brother Abel, becoming the first murderer (Genesis 4:8). God cursed him to be a fugitive and vagabond, yet set a mark upon him to protect his life; he went out from the presence of the LORD to the land of Nod and built a city (Genesis 4:11-17).

He is called 'the father of Canaan,' and when he saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers, Noah pronounced a curse upon Canaan (Genesis 9:22-25). From Ham descended Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan, the ancestors of many nations including Egypt and the peoples of Canaan (Genesis 10:6).

kids.disambig: son of Eliab, a Reubenite; with his brother Abiram, joined Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron and was swallowed by the earth

kids.name: Nemuel
kids.disambig: son of Eliab, a Reubenite; brother of Dathan and Abiram -- a real, distinct individual from Simeon's own son Jemuel, who is ALSO called 'Nemuel' at Numbers 26:12, a genuine same-name collision within this same chapter

BIBLE:Jacob.name: Simeon
BIBLE:Jacob.disambig: second son of Jacob and Leah

kids.name: Jachin
kids.disambig: son of Simeon

kids.name: Jamin
kids.disambig: son of Simeon

kids.name: Jemuel
kids.disambig: son of Simeon

kids.name: Ohad
kids.disambig: son of Simeon

kids.name: Shaul
kids.disambig: son of Simeon and a Canaanite woman (unnamed in the text); distinct from Saul king of Edom (Genesis 36:37) and the later King Saul of Israel

kids.name: Zohar
kids.disambig: son of Simeon; distinct from Zohar father of Ephron the Hittite (Genesis 23:8)

BIBLE:Jacob.name: Zebulun
BIBLE:Jacob.bio: Zebulun is the tenth son of Jacob and the sixth by Leah, who named him hoping her husband would dwell with her (Genesis 30:20). He is the founder of the tribe of Zebulun. Jacob prophesied, 'Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; and he shall be for an haven of ships' (Genesis 49:13).

kids.name: Elon
kids.disambig: son of Zebulun; distinct from Elon the Hittite, father of Bashemath (Genesis 26:34)

kids.name: Jahleel
kids.disambig: son of Zebulun

kids.name: Sered
kids.disambig: son of Zebulun

BIBLE:Judah.name: Onan
BIBLE:Judah.bio: Onan is the second son of Judah by the daughter of Shua (Genesis 38:4). Commanded to raise up seed for his dead brother Er by Tamar, he refused to fulfill the duty and spilled his seed on the ground; this displeased the LORD, who slew him (Genesis 38:8-10).

BIBLE:Judah.name: Shelah
BIBLE:Judah.disambig: son of Judah; distinct from Shelah son of Arphaxad (Genesis 10:24, 11:12-15, called Salah in this catalogue's own Phase 1/2 entries -- same underlying name, different real individual)
BIBLE:Judah.bio: Shelah is the third son of Judah by the daughter of Shua, born at Chezib (Genesis 38:5). Judah withheld him from marrying the widowed Tamar, fearing he too would die (Genesis 38:11). He became the ancestor of the Shelanite family of Judah (Numbers 26:20).

BIBLE:Judah.name: Zarah
BIBLE:Judah.disambig: son of Judah and Tamar, twin of Pharez
BIBLE:Judah.bio: Zarah (Zerah) is a son of Judah by Tamar and the twin of Pharez; at the birth his hand came out first and was bound with a scarlet thread, but his brother 'broke forth' before him (Genesis 38:27-30). He is known chiefly for this notable birth and as an ancestral head within Judah.

kids.name: Zabdi
kids.disambig: son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah; father of Carmi; distinct from other men named Zabdi later in the KJV text (e.g. 1 Chronicles 8:19, 27:27)

kids.name: Carmi
kids.disambig: son of Zabdi, of the tribe of Judah; father of Achan; distinct from Carmi son of Reuben (Genesis 46:9, Phase 4), a real, unrelated name-reuse across two different tribes

kids.name: Achan
kids.disambig: son of Carmi, of the tribe of Judah; took accursed spoil from Jericho and was stoned for it

BIBLE:Pharez.name: Hamul
BIBLE:Pharez.disambig: son of Pharez, grandson of Judah
BIBLE:Pharez.bio: Hamul is a son of Pharez and grandson of Judah, who went down into Egypt among Jacob's household (Genesis 46:12). He became the head of the Hamulites family of Judah (Numbers 26:21). Beyond this genealogical note, no further deeds are recorded of him.

BIBLE:Amminadab.name: Elisheba
BIBLE:Amminadab.disambig: daughter of Amminadab; sister of Naashon; Aaron's wife
BIBLE:Amminadab.bio: Elisheba is the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Naashon, who became the wife of Aaron the high priest (Exodus 6:23). She was the mother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, and thus the matriarch of the Aaronic priesthood.

BIBLE:Jesse.name: Abinadab
BIBLE:Jesse.disambig: second son of Jesse; David's brother; distinct from Saul's own son Abinadab (1 Samuel 31:2) and from Abinadab of Kirjath-jearim (1 Samuel 7:1) -- a real triple name-reuse
BIBLE:Jesse.bio: Abinadab is the second son of Jesse, who passed before Samuel but was not chosen as king (1 Samuel 16:8). He was among the three eldest sons of Jesse who followed Saul to the battle against the Philistines (1 Samuel 17:13). He is a brother of David.

BIBLE:Jesse.name: Eliab
BIBLE:Jesse.disambig: eldest son of Jesse; David's brother; a real THIRD 'Eliab' alongside Eliab son of Helon (Numbers 1:9) and Eliab son of Pallu (Numbers 26:8, both Phase 6)
BIBLE:Jesse.bio: Eliab is the eldest son of Jesse, so impressive in appearance that Samuel thought him the LORD's anointed, but God said, 'Look not on his countenance... for the LORD looketh on the heart' (1 Samuel 16:6-7). He rebuked David for coming to the battlefield before David fought Goliath (1 Samuel 17:28). He is David's eldest brother.

BIBLE:Jesse.name: Shammah
BIBLE:Jesse.disambig: third son of Jesse; David's brother; possibly (not certainly) the same real man as Shammah, one of David's own mighty men (2 Samuel 23:11, not yet catalogued)
BIBLE:Jesse.bio: Shammah is the third son of Jesse, who passed before Samuel but was not chosen (1 Samuel 16:9). He was among the three eldest sons who followed Saul to war against the Philistines (1 Samuel 17:13). He is a brother of David.

kids.name: Jonadab
kids.disambig: son of Shammah/Shimeah, David's brother; a subtil man; advised Amnon

BIBLE:David.name: Solomon
BIBLE:David.disambig: son of David and Bathsheba; Israel's third king
BIBLE:David.bio: Solomon is the son of David and Bathsheba who succeeded his father as king over Israel (2 Samuel 12:24, 1 Kings 1-2). Granted extraordinary wisdom by God, he judged wisely, spoke thousands of proverbs, and wrote songs (1 Kings 3-4). He built the temple in Jerusalem and reigned over a kingdom of unmatched wealth and peace, yet in his old age his many foreign wives turned his heart to other gods (1 Kings 6, 11). He is the ancestor of the kings of Judah in Matthew's genealogy.

kids.name: Rehoboam
kids.disambig: son of Solomon and Naamah the Ammonitess; his harshness split the kingdom, keeping only Judah

kids.name: Abijam
kids.disambig: son of Rehoboam; reigned three years over Judah

kids.name: Asa
kids.disambig: son of Abijam; reigned forty-one years over Judah

kids.name: Jehoshaphat
kids.disambig: son of Asa; reigned over Judah; distinct from Jehoshaphat the recorder under David (2 Samuel 8:16, Phase 10)

kids.name: Jehoram
kids.disambig: son of Jehoshaphat; king of Judah; married Athaliah, Ahab's daughter; distinct from Jehoram son of Ahab, king of Israel -- his own contemporary and brother-in-law

kids.name: Ahaziah
kids.disambig: son of Jehoram, king of Judah; distinct from Ahaziah son of Ahab, king of Israel (1 Kings 22:51, Phase 11)

kids.name: Joash
kids.disambig: son of Ahaziah, king of Judah; hidden as an infant by Jehosheba; crowned king at seven by Jehoiada the priest; distinct from Joash, a later king of Israel (2 Kings 13:10)

kids.name: Amaziah
kids.disambig: son of Joash, king of Judah; distinct from Amaziah, priest of Bethel under Jeroboam II (Amos 7:10, not yet catalogued)

kids.name: Jehosheba
kids.disambig: daughter of king Joram (Jehoram of Judah); sister of Ahaziah; hid the infant Joash from Athaliah

BIBLE:David.name: Absalom
BIBLE:David.disambig: David's third son, of Maacah; killed Amnon; later rebelled against David and was killed by Joab
BIBLE:David.bio: Absalom is the third son of David, born to Maacah, renowned for his beauty and his abundant hair (2 Samuel 3:3, 14:25-26). He killed his brother Amnon to avenge his sister Tamar, then led a rebellion that drove David from Jerusalem (2 Samuel 13, 15). He was caught by his head in an oak during the battle and slain by Joab, provoking David's bitter lament, 'O my son Absalom' (2 Samuel 18:9-33).

kids.name: Maachah
kids.disambig: daughter of Abishalom (a real, disclosed spelling variant of Absalom, 2 Samuel 3:3) -- making her Absalom's own granddaughter and David's own great-granddaughter; mother (or, on the loose usage of 1 Kings 15:10, possibly grandmother) of both Abijam and Asa; distinct from Maacah, David's own wife and Absalom's mother (2 Samuel 3:3, Phase 10)

BIBLE:David.name: Adonijah
BIBLE:David.bio: Adonijah is the fourth son of David, born to Haggith (2 Samuel 3:4). He exalted himself to be king in David's old age, but the throne was given to Solomon (1 Kings 1). After David's death he requested Abishag the Shunammite as wife, and Solomon, seeing this as a bid for the throne, had him put to death (1 Kings 2:13-25).

BIBLE:David.name: Amnon
BIBLE:David.disambig: David's firstborn, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; later raped his half-sister Tamar and was killed by Absalom
BIBLE:David.bio: Amnon is the firstborn son of David, born to Ahinoam of Jezreel (2 Samuel 3:2). He violated his half-sister Tamar, and for this crime her brother Absalom had him killed two years later at a sheepshearing feast (2 Samuel 13). His death set in motion Absalom's estrangement and later revolt.

BIBLE:David.name: Chileab
BIBLE:David.disambig: David's second son, of Abigail, Nabal's widow
BIBLE:David.bio: Chileab (also called Daniel) is the second son of David, born to Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite (2 Samuel 3:3). He is known only from this genealogical listing of David's sons, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Eliada
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem
BIBLE:David.bio: Eliada is a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:16). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Eliphalet
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem
BIBLE:David.bio: Eliphalet is a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:16). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Elishama
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem; distinct from Elishama son of Ammihud (Numbers 1:10, Phase 6)
BIBLE:David.bio: Elishama is a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:16). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Elishua
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem
BIBLE:David.bio: Elishua is a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:15). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Ibhar
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem
BIBLE:David.bio: Ibhar is a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:15). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Ithream
BIBLE:David.bio: Ithream is the sixth son of David, born in Hebron to David's wife Eglah (2 Samuel 3:5). He is known only from this listing of David's sons, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Japhia
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem
BIBLE:David.bio: Japhia is a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:15). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Nepheg
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem; distinct from Nepheg son of Izhar (Exodus 6:21, Phase 5)
BIBLE:David.bio: Nepheg is a son of David born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:15). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Shammuah
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem
BIBLE:David.bio: Shammuah (Shammua) is a son of David and Bathsheba born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:14). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Shephatiah
BIBLE:David.bio: Shephatiah is the fifth son of David, born in Hebron to David's wife Abital (2 Samuel 3:4). He is known only from this listing of David's sons, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Shobab
BIBLE:David.disambig: a son of David, born in Jerusalem
BIBLE:David.bio: Shobab is a son of David and Bathsheba born in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:14). He is known only as one of David's sons in the genealogical list, with no further recorded deeds.

BIBLE:David.name: Tamar
BIBLE:David.disambig: David's daughter, Absalom's full sister; raped by her half-brother Amnon; distinct from Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law (Genesis 38, Phase 4)
BIBLE:David.bio: Tamar is the beautiful daughter of David and full sister of Absalom (2 Samuel 13:1). Her half-brother Amnon lured her under pretense of illness and violated her, then cast her out, and she remained desolate in her brother Absalom's house (2 Samuel 13:2-20). Her outrage led Absalom to kill Amnon in revenge.

families.name: Ammihud
families.disambig: of the tribe of Naphtali; father of Pedahel -- the third of a real, disclosed triple name-reuse; see Ammihud father of Elishama (Numbers 1:10) and Ammihud father of Shemuel (Numbers 34:20)

kids.name: Pedahel
kids.disambig: son of Ammihud; prince of the tribe of Naphtali appointed to divide the land

families.name: Benaiah
families.disambig: father of Pelatiah, one of twenty-five princes seen at the temple's east gate; distinct from the two other already-catalogued men named Benaiah (David's mighty man; ancestor of Jahaziel)

kids.name: Pelatiah
kids.disambig: son of Benaiah; one of twenty-five princes seen at the temple's east gate; his sudden death during Ezekiel's own prophesying provoked the prophet's recorded outcry (11:13); distinct from Pelatiah, son of Hananiah (1 Chronicles 3:21, Phase 13)

families.name: The Twelve Apostles
families.meaning: the twelve Yeshua chose and sent (Gk. apostoloi, 'sent ones')
families.disambig: the apostolic company around Yeshua the Christ
families.bio: The twelve apostles whom Yeshua the Christ chose to be with Him and to be sent out: Simon Peter and his brother Andrew; James and John the sons of Zebedee; Philip; Bartholomew (Nathanael); Thomas; Matthew the publican; James son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus (Judas of James); Simon the Zealot; and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Him and was replaced by Matthias.

kids.name: Peter
kids.meaning: Shim'on, 'he has heard'; surnamed Kepha / Petros, 'a rock'
kids.disambig: Simon Peter, first of the twelve apostles
kids.bio: Simon bar-Jonah, a fisherman of Bethsaida and Capernaum, called with his brother Andrew to be a 'fisher of men'; renamed Kepha (Peter, 'rock'). First-named of the twelve apostles of Yeshua, spokesman among them, who confessed Him the Christ, denied Him thrice, was restored, and led the early church.

kids.name: Andrew
kids.disambig: apostle, brother of Simon Peter
kids.bio: Brother of Simon Peter, a fisherman of Bethsaida and first a disciple of John the Baptist. An apostle of Yeshua; he brought Peter to the Lord and is remembered for bringing others to Him.

kids.name: James
kids.disambig: one of the twelve apostles; son of Zebedee; brother of John; distinct from James, son of Alphaeus

kids.name: John
kids.disambig: one of the twelve apostles; son of Zebedee; brother of James; distinct from John the Baptist

kids.name: Philip
kids.disambig: apostle of Bethsaida
kids.bio: An apostle of Yeshua from Bethsaida who brought Nathanael to Him ('come and see'); distinct from Philip the evangelist of Acts.

kids.name: Nathanael (Bartholomew)
kids.meaning: Netan'el, 'God has given'; also called Bartholomew, bar-Talmai ('son of Talmai')
kids.disambig: apostle, commonly identified with Bartholomew
kids.bio: An Israelite 'in whom is no guile' whom Yeshua saw under the fig tree; an apostle, commonly identified with Bartholomew (bar-Talmai).

kids.name: Thomas
kids.disambig: apostle called Didymus, the Twin
kids.bio: An apostle of Yeshua called Didymus, 'the Twin'; who doubted the resurrection until he saw and confessed 'My Lord and my God.'

kids.name: Matthew
kids.meaning: Mattityahu, 'gift of YHWH'; Levi the publican
kids.disambig: apostle and evangelist, son of Alphaeus (Levi)
kids.bio: Levi son of Alphaeus, a tax-collector (publican) at Capernaum called by Yeshua from the receipt of custom; an apostle and the evangelist to whom the first Gospel is ascribed.

kids.name: James
kids.disambig: one of the twelve apostles; son of Alphaeus; distinct from James, son of Zebedee

kids.name: Thaddaeus (Judas of James)
kids.disambig: apostle Jude / Thaddaeus
kids.bio: An apostle of Yeshua, Judas 'not Iscariot' (of James), also called Thaddaeus / Lebbaeus.

kids.name: Simon the Zealot
kids.meaning: Shim'on, 'he has heard'; the Zealot / Cananaean
kids.disambig: apostle, the Zealot
kids.bio: An apostle of Yeshua, called the Zealot (Cananaean), once of the zealot party.

kids.name: Judas Iscariot
kids.disambig: the apostle who betrayed Yeshua
kids.bio: Son of Simon Iscariot; the apostle and treasurer of the twelve who betrayed Yeshua for thirty pieces of silver and perished.

families.name: Abdeel
families.disambig: father of Shelemiah, one of the men commanded to seize Baruch and Jeremiah

kids.name: Shelemiah
kids.disambig: son of Abdeel; one of the men commanded to seize Baruch and Jeremiah; one of at least four real, distinct men named Shelemiah in this book

families.name: Gershom
families.disambig: a Levite; father of Jonathan, priest to the tribe of Dan (Judges 18:30) -- the real KJV text names his own father 'Manasseh,' a famous textual crux: many Hebrew manuscripts write a suspended letter nun there, widely read by scholars as an editorial disguise for 'Moses,' to avoid recording that Moses's own descendants served an idolatrous shrine. This project follows the real KJV text as printed rather than the emendation, and keeps this Gershom distinct from Moses's own son Gershom (Exodus 2:22, Phase 5) rather than silently identifying them

kids.name: Jonathan
kids.disambig: son of Gershom the Levite; became priest to the graven image at Dan; distinct from the far more famous later Jonathan, Saul's son (not yet catalogued)

families.name: Mary
families.disambig: mother of Jesus; espoused to Joseph; found with child of the Holy Ghost; distinct from the several other Marys named later in this same book

kids.name: Jesus
kids.disambig: son of Mary and (legally) Joseph; called Emmanuel (1:23, quoting Isaiah 7:14, Phase 21) and Christ; the central figure of the New Testament

families.name: Machi
families.disambig: father of Geuel, the spy from Gad

kids.name: Geuel
kids.disambig: son of Machi; spy sent from the tribe of Gad

families.name: Gideoni
families.disambig: father of Abidan, prince of Benjamin

kids.name: Abidan
kids.disambig: son of Gideoni; prince of the tribe of Benjamin

families.name: Ahilud
families.disambig: father of Jehoshaphat the recorder

kids.name: Jehoshaphat
kids.disambig: son of Ahilud; recorder under David; distinct from the later King Jehoshaphat of Judah (1 Kings 15, not yet catalogued)

families.name: Ammiel
families.disambig: father of Machir of Lo-debar; distinct from Ammiel son of Gemalli (Numbers 13:12, Phase 6)

kids.name: Machir
kids.disambig: son of Ammiel, of Lo-debar; sheltered Mephibosheth and later provisioned David; distinct from Machir son of Manasseh (Numbers 26:29, Phase 6)

families.name: Habaziniah
families.disambig: grandfather of Jaazaniah, head of the Rechabites in Jeremiah's own day

kids.name: Jeremiah
kids.disambig: son of Habaziniah; father of Jaazaniah, head of the Rechabites -- a real, distinct man from Jeremiah the prophet and from Jeremiah of Libnah, father of Hamutal

kids.name: Jaazaniah
kids.disambig: son of Jeremiah, son of Habaziniah; head of the house of the Rechabites tested by the prophet Jeremiah; distinct from Jaazaniah, son of a Maachathite (2 Kings 25:23, Phase 12)

families.name: Gera
families.disambig: a Benjamite; father of Ehud; distinct from Gera, a literal son of Benjamin four centuries earlier (Genesis 46:21, Phase 4)

kids.name: Ehud
kids.disambig: son of Gera, a Benjamite, left-handed; Israel's second judge; killed Eglon king of Moab

families.name: Remaliah
families.disambig: father of Pekah, king of Israel

kids.name: Pekah
kids.disambig: son of Remaliah; king of Israel; slain by Hoshea

families.name: Zeruiah
families.disambig: mother of Joab, Abishai, and Asahel; elsewhere named as David's own sister (1 Chronicles 2:16, not yet catalogued)

kids.name: Abishai
kids.disambig: son of Zeruiah; one of David's chief warriors

kids.name: Asahel
kids.disambig: son of Zeruiah; noted for his swiftness of foot

kids.name: Joab
kids.disambig: son of Zeruiah; commander of David's army

families.name: Omri
families.disambig: reigned twelve years over Israel; father of Ahab

kids.name: Ahab
kids.disambig: son of Omri; reigned twenty-two years over Israel in Samaria

kids.name: Ahaziah
kids.disambig: son of Ahab; reigned two years over Israel

kids.name: Athaliah
kids.disambig: daughter of Ahab; mother of Ahaziah, king of Judah; seized the throne and destroyed the royal seed after her son's death, save for the infant Joash

kids.name: Jehoram
kids.disambig: son of Ahab; king of Israel; reigned after his brother Ahaziah died without a son; distinct from Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah -- his own contemporary and brother-in-law through Athaliah -- a real, disclosed name collision between two kings reigning at once

families.name: Jehoiada
families.disambig: the priest who hid, crowned, and covenanted with Joash; distinct from Jehoiada, father of Benaiah under David (2 Samuel 8:18, Phase 10)

kids.name: Zechariah
kids.disambig: son of Jehoiada the priest, who had crowned Joash (2 Kings 11:4, Phase 12); prophesied against Judah's own apostasy and was stoned to death by Joash's own command

families.name: Parnach
families.disambig: father of Elizaphan, prince of Zebulun

kids.name: Elizaphan
kids.disambig: son of Parnach; prince of the tribe of Zebulun appointed to divide the land; distinct from Elzaphan/Elizaphan son of Uzziel, chief of the Kohathites (Exodus 6:22, Numbers 3:30)

families.name: Ebed
families.disambig: father of Gaal

kids.name: Gaal
kids.disambig: son of Ebed; rallied Shechem against Abimelech

families.name: Nun
families.disambig: father of Joshua, of the tribe of Ephraim

kids.name: Joshua
kids.disambig: military leader under Moses; his own fuller introduction and genealogy come later, outside Genesis/Exodus

families.name: Ammishaddai
families.disambig: father of Ahiezer, prince of Dan

kids.name: Ahiezer
kids.disambig: son of Ammishaddai; prince of the tribe of Dan

families.name: Mattaniah
families.disambig: ancestor of Jahaziel the Levite prophet; distinct from Mattaniah, King Zedekiah's own birth name (2 Kings 24:17, Phase 12), a real, unrelated name-reuse

kids.name: Jeiel
kids.disambig: son of Mattaniah; ancestor of Jahaziel the Levite prophet

kids.name: Benaiah
kids.disambig: son of Jeiel; ancestor of Jahaziel the Levite prophet; distinct from Benaiah son of Jehoiada, David's own captain (2 Samuel 8:18, Phase 10)

kids.name: Zechariah
kids.disambig: son of Benaiah; father of Jahaziel the Levite prophet

kids.name: Jahaziel
kids.disambig: son of Zechariah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph; the Spirit of the LORD came upon him and he prophesied victory for Jehoshaphat over Moab and Ammon

families.name: Shemaiah
families.disambig: of Kirjathjearim; father of Urijah, a prophet killed by Jehoiakim; distinct from Shemaiah the Nehelamite and from Shemaiah, father of Delaiah

kids.name: Urijah
kids.disambig: son of Shemaiah of Kirjathjearim; a prophet who prophesied against Jerusalem in the same words as Jeremiah, fled to Egypt, and was brought back and killed by Jehoiakim; distinct from Uriah the Hittite (Phase 9/10) and Uriah the priest (Isaiah 8:2, Phase 21)

families.name: Potipherah
families.disambig: priest of On; father of Asenath; distinct spelling from Potiphar the captain of the guard (Genesis 37:36) -- the real similarity is disclosed, not resolved as the same man

kids.name: Asenath
kids.disambig: daughter of Potipherah; Joseph's wife

families.name: Herod
families.disambig: king of Judaea at the birth of Jesus; sought to kill the young child; ordered the slaughter of the children of Bethlehem; father of Archelaus; distinct from the several other Herods named later in the New Testament

kids.name: Archelaus
kids.disambig: son of Herod the Great; reigned in Judaea in his father's stead

families.name: Chislon
families.disambig: father of Elidad, prince of Benjamin

kids.name: Elidad
kids.disambig: son of Chislon; prince of the tribe of Benjamin appointed to divide the land

families.name: Amittai
families.disambig: father of Jonah the prophet

kids.name: Jonah
kids.disambig: the prophet; son of Amittai, of Gathhepher; already named as a real historical prophet under Jeroboam II in 2 Kings 14:25 (Phase 12), but never catalogued there -- a real, disclosed retroactive gap-fill

families.name: Talmai
families.disambig: king of Geshur; father of Maacah

kids.name: Maacah
kids.disambig: daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur; David's wife; mother of Absalom

families.name: Buzi
families.disambig: father of Ezekiel the prophet, of the priests

kids.name: Ezekiel
kids.disambig: the priest; son of Buzi; received his prophetic call by the river Chebar in the land of the Chaldeans

families.name: Aphiah
families.disambig: a Benjamite; ancestor of Kish and Saul

kids.name: Bechorath
kids.disambig: son of Aphiah; ancestor of Kish and Saul

kids.name: Zeror
kids.disambig: son of Bechorath; ancestor of Kish and Saul

kids.name: Abiel
kids.disambig: son of Zeror; father of BOTH Kish (Saul's father) and Ner (Abner's father, 1 Samuel 14:51) -- making Saul and Abner real first cousins, which is why 1 Samuel 14:50 loosely calls Abner 'Saul's uncle' in the KJV's own wording

kids.name: Kish
kids.disambig: son of Abiel, a Benjamite; father of Saul

kids.name: Saul
